mechanism: Additive anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects
management: Avoid combination unless specifically indicated. Monitor for signs of bleeding.

mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and may cause GI bleeding; combined with anticoagulant effect of warfarin
clinical_effect: Increased risk of GI bleeding and hemorrhage
management: Avoid NSAIDs if possible. Use acetaminophen for pain. If NSAID required, use lowest dose for shortest duration and add GI protection.

mechanism: Contrast media can cause acute kidney injury, leading to metformin accumulation and lactic acidosis
management: Withhold metformin 48 hours before and after contrast administration. Check renal function before restarting.

mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone secretion, decreasing potassium excretion
management: Monitor serum potassium regularly. Avoid potassium supplements unless documented hypokalemia.

mechanism: Both drugs independently increase serum potassium
management: Monitor potassium closely (within 1 week of initiation, then regularly). Start spironolactone at low dose.

mechanism: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin levels
clinical_effect: Increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
management: Limit simvastatin dose to 20mg/day when co-administered with amlodipine.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate
clinical_effect: Methotrexate toxicity (bone marrow suppression, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity)
management: Avoid NSAIDs with high-dose methotrexate. With low-dose, use with extreme caution and monitor.

mechanism: Both increase serotonin levels via different mechanisms
management: Avoid combination. If essential, start at lowest doses and monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms.

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, reducing theophylline metabolism
management: Reduce theophylline dose by 30-50%. Monitor serum theophylline levels.

mechanism: Clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, dramatically increasing statin levels
management: Contraindicated. Suspend statin during clarithromycin course or use azithromycin instead.

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to its active metabolite
clinical_effect: Reduced antiplatelet effect, increased cardiovascular risk
management: Use pantoprazole instead (does not significantly inhibit CYP2C19).

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and renal clearance of digoxin
management: Reduce digoxin dose by 50% when starting amiodarone. Monitor digoxin levels.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance
management: Avoid NSAIDs if possible. If required, monitor lithium levels and reduce dose.

mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9, the primary enzyme metabolizing warfarin
clinical_effect: Dramatically increased INR, high bleeding risk
management: Reduce warfarin dose by 25-50%. Monitor INR within 3-5 days. Consider alternative antifungal.

mechanism: Warfarin may displace sulfonylureas from protein binding and inhibit their metabolism
clinical_effect: Enhanced hypoglycemic effect, increased risk of severe hypoglycemia
management: Monitor blood glucose more frequently. Adjust glipizide dose as needed.

mechanism: Alcohol potentiates the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism
management: Advise patients to limit alcohol consumption while on metformin.

mechanism: Additive antihypertensive effect
management: Commonly used together intentionally. Monitor blood pressure. Start one agent at a time.

mechanism: Additive hypoglycemic effect via different mechanisms
management: Common combination. Monitor blood glucose regularly. Educate patient on hypoglycemia signs.

mechanism: Amlodipine mildly inhibits CYP3A4, increasing atorvastatin exposure ~18%
management: Generally safe. Consider limiting atorvastatin to 40mg if combining. Monitor for muscle symptoms.

mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effects via different pathways
management: Often used together intentionally (dual antiplatelet therapy post-stent). Monitor for bleeding.

mechanism: Additive hypotensive effect; ACE inhibitors can potentiate diuretic-induced dehydration
management: Start ACE inhibitor at low dose. Monitor blood pressure and electrolytes.

mechanism: SSRIs impair platelet aggregation; NSAIDs cause GI mucosal damage
clinical_effect: Increased risk of GI bleeding (3-15x higher than either alone)
management: Add gastroprotection (PPI) if combination required. Consider acetaminophen instead.

mechanism: Loop diuretics can impair renal function and cause dehydration
clinical_effect: Increased risk of lactic acidosis due to reduced renal clearance of metformin
management: Monitor renal function regularly. Ensure adequate hydration.

mechanism: Both corticosteroids and NSAIDs increase GI ulceration risk independently
clinical_effect: Significantly increased risk of GI bleeding and peptic ulcer
management: Add PPI gastroprotection. Use lowest effective doses for shortest duration.

mechanism: Both lower blood glucose via different mechanisms
management: Close glucose monitoring. Reduce sulfonylurea dose when adding insulin.

mechanism: Calcium binds levothyroxine in the GI tract, reducing absorption
clinical_effect: Reduced thyroid hormone efficacy, potential hypothyroidism symptoms
management: Separate administration by at least 4 hours. Take levothyroxine on empty stomach.

mechanism: PPIs increase gastric pH, reducing levothyroxine absorption
management: Monitor TSH levels. May need to increase levothyroxine dose.

mechanism: Aspirin may slightly reduce the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors
management: Generally clinically insignificant at low-dose aspirin (81mg). Monitor blood pressure.
